name: Place Stanislas, Place de la Carrière and Place d'Alliance in Nancy
description: In the heart of Nancy, in eastern France, three linked squares were built between 1752 and 1756 for Stanislas Leszczynski, the exiled Polish king who became Duke of Lorraine. Architect Emmanuel Héré tied them into one grand walkway, from the pedestrianised Place Stanislas to the tree-lined Place de la Carrière and on to the Place d'Alliance. Together they made a royal showpiece that also worked as a lively civic space.
